issue: The annual saving has lost its minus sign. The source low saving is negative (-£1.5126 per pack: aerogel costs more), and the per-pack string keeps it, but annualSaving and costSavingPotential.annualValue read '£181.5K-£36.3K', which shows a £181.5K GAIN where the source states a £181.5K COST.
evidence: Ideas row ID-018: Saving low -1.5126, Saving high 0.3025. Record perVehicle '£-1.51-£0.30 per pack'; annualSaving '£181.5K-£36.3K at 120,000 packs/yr'. The text itself says 'this idea spends money'.
recommendation: Render it as '-£181.5K to £36.3K' (or 'cost £181.5K to save £36.3K'), and fix the generator for every negative band in the pack.

issue: Converter artefacts in costSavingPotential.calculationBasis, on every Not selected / Hold / Screened-out idea in the slice: 'payback None yrs' (a Python None leaking into text), and 'NRE £0' where the Evaluation cell is BLANK, not zero. A blank means NRE was not assessed for an idea that was not selected. It does not mean free.
evidence: e.g. ID-002 calculationBasis: 'Evaluation risk-adjusted: £2.65-£4.42 per pack at p 0.5; NRE £0; payback None yrs.' Evaluation row ID-002: NRE GBP '', Payback yrs ''. Its investmentText says 'of the order of 200k GBP combined'.
recommendation: Write 'NRE not assessed (not selected)' and drop the payback clause when the source cell is blank.

issue: Two items are not carried into the records. (a) The five Evaluation criterion scores (Saving potential, Technical feasibility, Investment required, Lead time, Specification and safety risk); only the weighted total is kept. (b) Level is re-labelled 'sub-assembly'->'subassembly' and 'component'->'part'. The re-labelling is a vocabulary mapping, not a loss. Every other field matched the source exactly for all 76 ideas: title, all 10 text columns, affected GBP, saving low/high, depth, group, lever, novelty, maturity, effort, lead time, conflicts, saving basis, decision, reason, weighted score, p, risk-adjusted low/high, NRE, shared NRE, payback and NRE note. The Ideas 'Saving low/high' also equal the Evaluation 'Saving low/high' for every idea.
evidence: Scripted cell-by-cell comparison of 'Ideas' rows 5-80 and the matching 'Evaluation' rows against slice-48V-A.json.
recommendation: Optional: add the five criterion scores to ideaData, so a reader can see why an idea was selected.

issue: The claimed saving is larger than the only cost line that actually falls. This is the top-ranked Develop idea (weighted 4.73). It saves thermal adhesive: the content is £3.78, and the mechanism's own arithmetic is 'about £1.70'. The band of £4.60-£8.74 (risk-adjusted £3.91-£7.43) is reached only by counting the £19.21 A380 housing in the affected cost. But the idea makes the housing MORE expensive (flatness control or machining, which the risk text acknowledges). The high case is 2.3x the entire adhesive line and 5x the stated mechanism.
evidence: Parts: Thermal conductive adhesive 0.42 kg £3.78; Housing A380 £19.21. ID-011 Mechanism: 'Halving the design gap roughly halves the dispensed mass, about £1.70'. Risk: 'if the floor has to be machined the operation may cost more than the adhesive it saves'. Saving low/high 4.598/8.7362 on affected £22.99.
recommendation: Show the saving as unverified or overstated in front of the Director. The study's own deck (slide 4) warns that the bands are overstated. Do not quote £4.60-£8.74 per pack or the implied £0.55M-£1.05M a year.

issue: The claimed saving is larger than the content the idea can remove. Cell-to-pack deletes the frame, cover and plate parts; it does not change the cell. Yet the £122.41 cell is in the £135.02 affected cost. The non-cell content affected is £12.61, and even the LOW saving (£16.20) exceeds it, as does the risk-adjusted high (£16.20). No arithmetic is given, and the benchmark admits 'No published 48V cell-to-pack benchmark was found'.
evidence: Deck slide 14 'What we do today': cells £122.41; side plates £2.20; end plates £2.60; tie rods £0.90; stack cover £1.10; top insulation plate £0.55; + busbars £5.26 = £135.02. Saving low/high £16.20-£32.40.
recommendation: Show it as unverified. At most the £12.61 non-cell content (less the added housing tooling cost) can be at stake, unless the author shows a cell-price mechanism.

issue: The saving band is not derived from the stated mechanism. The itemised deletions total about £4.8 (plugs £0.70, impregnation £1.20, port parts £2.74, glycol £0.18), plus some adhesive. Reaching £11.18-£17.03 needs a £4-£10 fall in the £19.21 casting, while fins and a dearer alloy are added and a dearer 75 degC cell returns 'part of the saving at the largest line'. That penalty is not netted. The high saving (£17.03) also exceeds the £12.84 value-gap cap the text itself states.
evidence: Mechanism: 'two plugs at £0.70 and the vacuum impregnation at £1.20 ... coolant interface parts go at £2.74; the glycol charge goes at £0.18'. Risk: 'A 75 degC-capable cell also costs more per kWh ... part of the saving returns at the largest line.' Value gap £12.84.
recommendation: Present it as an architecture decision (deck Decision 1, 'confirm why the pack is liquid cooled'), not as a quoted saving.

issue: Double-counting between two Develop ideas. ID-001 'reduce[s] the adhesive to a controlled thin bond line', and ID-011 (Develop) cuts the same £3.78 adhesive. Both also claim the housing. evidence: ID-001 Specifics: 'reduce the adhesive to a controlled thin bond line'; ID-011: 'cut the thermal interface material volume'. Both list 'Thermal conductive adhesive; Housing, A380 die casting'.
recommendation: Add a conflict edge, or net the overlap. Report to the author.

issue: A logical contradiction inside the Develop list. Carrying over a BMS from another 48V application replaces the board design. Yet four other Develop ideas redesign the same £40 board: ID-059 (new 12S front end), ID-060 (delete unused channels), ID-063 (4- to 2-layer re-lay) and ID-064 (re-panelise). None of them shares a conflict set with ID-062 (C11). On that one £40.00 board the Develop high savings sum to £32.00 (risk-adjusted £22.48), which exceeds its £25.63 value gap. The benchmark is also weak: Hella's PowerPack is an integrated battery+BMS+DC/DC block, not evidence of BMS carry-over across applications, and the same benchmark is cited for the opposite move (ID-003, integration).
recommendation: Report to the author: either ID-062 or the redesign ideas, not both.

issue: The mechanism does not apply to this pack as stated. A 12S1P string cannot buy 'less cell': the cell count is fixed by voltage, so a usable-capacity gain only pays if a smaller-Ah cell is specified. That is a new cell, which is inconsistent with 'Low' effort, NRE £0 and 12-18 months. The risk text also says the saving 'is not obvious', yet p success is 0.85. The idea reaches Develop through the 1%-of-BOM route on that p.
evidence: Mechanism: 'less cell has to be bought for the same usable energy'. Risk: 'The saving only appears if the usable-capacity gain exceeds the sorting premium, which is not obvious.' p 0.85; Reason: 'risk-adjusted saving of £6.24 is at or above 1 per cent'.
recommendation: Flag p and the mechanism to the author. Show it as unverified.

issue: The status contradicts the text. The risk text says a latching relay 'cannot be switched under fault current as fast as a semiconductor, which is exactly what DO-09 asks for' (it fails a stated design objective), yet the idea is Develop at p 0.7 with 'Production elsewhere' maturity and 'No published benchmark'. The cost premise (a relay is cheaper than a MOSFET array at 48V) is the reverse of the existing library idea lux-f13407b63bdf, where a MOSFET switch replaces a relay in a 48V battery. The high saving (£1.44) also exceeds its £0.81 gap cap.
evidence: ID-066 Risk text as quoted. Library marketplace-luxury-suv-mhev-bev-ideas.json lux-f13407b63bdf 'Back-to-back MOSFET switch replaces electromechanical relay in 48V battery'.
recommendation: Show it as unverified, conflicting with a design objective. Raise it with the author.

issue: Physics wording error. The mechanism says 'equal stiffness needs less than proportionally more thickness'. For equal plate bending stiffness, steel (E=210 GPa) needs about 0.69x the thickness of aluminium (E=70 GPa), i.e. thinner, which is what the title says ('at reduced thickness'). Mass is about 2x.
recommendation: Correct the sentence.
